mainEntity.name: How much does a Hyundai i30 N 2.0 T-GDi engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full rebuilt or reconditioned engine replacement for a Hyundai i30 N 2.0 T-GDi typically ranges from £2,500 to £4,000 for supply only, depending on the specialist and the extent of performance upgrades included. Used engines start around £1,000 but carry higher risk, while rebuilt units include upgraded components and a 12-month warranty.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of a failing G4KJ engine in a Hyundai i30 N 2.0 T-GDi?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common early warning signs in the Hyundai i30 N 2.0 T-GDi are increased oil consumption between services, noticeable turbo lag or whining noises, and occasional misfires under heavy load. You should also watch for illuminated engine management lights or blue exhaust smoke.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Hyundai i30 N 2.0 T-GDi?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. A well-maintained Hyundai i30 N 2.0 T-GDi holds a UK market value of £15,000-£25,000+, making a £2,500-£4,000 rebuilt engine a financially sound investment that preserves the vehicle's performance, track capability, and strong resale value for years to come.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Hyundai i30 N 2.0 T-GDi engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A professional supply and fit service for a Hyundai i30 N 2.0 T-GDi typically takes 2 to 4 days, depending on the specialist's workload and whether any ancillary components like the turbo or cooling system are being upgraded simultaneously. Sourcing a quality rebuilt unit may add a few days.

mainEntity.name: Can I fit a standard i30 engine in my i30 N 2.0 T-GDi?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The i30 N G4KJ engine features specific internal components, a larger turbocharger, revised pistons, and unique ECU mapping compared to standard i30 engines. Attempting to fit a non-N engine will result in severe performance loss and compatibility issues.

historyTimeline.h2: Hyundai i30 N 2.0 T-GDi - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: When the Hyundai i30 N launched, the 2.0 T-GDi badge marked the pinnacle of the i30 range, bringing a purpose-built, high-output turbocharged inline-4 engine designed for track-focused performance and daily drivability.

milestones.description: Introduction of the G4KJ 2.0L T-GDi engine (275 hp / 353 Nm) in the first-generation (PDe) i30 N, featuring a twin-scroll turbocharger and an electronically controlled wastegate.
Power output increased to 280 hp (CN7 generation) with revised engine mapping, a larger turbocharger, and an integrated electronic limited-slip differential (e-LSD) for enhanced track performance.
